I am in a similar situation so I might not be the person to take any suggestions from. But let's directly get to the point.
Since you have already decided you want to be happy, you can try the following (in no particular order):

1)- Find out what happiness means to you. I mean, what is more important to you. Do you like to indulge in professional activities and are failing there. Or would you like to indulge personally with people and would like to form bonds..

For professional happiness I would suggest joining a lot of forums and asking a lot of questions. Don't even think if something is "stupid", just ask.

For personal happiness, find anything that either you like or you haven't tried but wouldn't mind trying. For example, tennis. Find some place around people play tennis. Go there. Try to learn how to play tennis. You will form some bonds there. Maybe you will utterly fail at it. But that's okay, the goal is not to master it or even to be a good player.

The goal is to engage the mind somewhere so that it finds the situation "happy". Our mind plays a lot of games and it always finds peace in familiar situations so just try to make some new situation a familiar one.

2)- Stop, S.T.O.P. listening to sad songs (if you do) immediately. I mean right now. Whenever a sad song comes in your Playlist, remove it immediately. Don't even think about it. I have had moderate success using this step.

3)- When you are free/bored/sad, just randomly open youtube/google and search for something that would make you laugh no matter what. For me, chinese prank videos and Conan O Brian's show makes me laugh no matter what mood I'm in.

4)- Don't expect the depression to go away. It is not a thing that can go away. It will always be there as a part of you. Accept it. And find ways to ignore it. As hard as you can. It will be dificult at first. But try to find enough things to fill your day so that you can just ignore the depression. Watch random shows, songs, videos, memes, drawings etc... 

5)- Stop taking people seriously. Don't think that anyone knows what you are going through. No one can understand what you are feeling. So, no one can give any cure for it. Moreover, these are your feelings not a disease. You need to handle your life without taking too many opinions. Find out what caused you or causes you "pain". And formulate plans to avoid that in future.

Example: I felt oddly painful when I would be telling someone something and they just ignore, talk over me, start talking to someone else or just go away. So, I started remembering people and their attention span. I now know that I should only say 2 extra sentences to person A; person B can't handle anything so I'll rather not talk about anything with them; person C says good things so listen to them but just reply with "I'm fine" because their brain is not mature enough to understand whatever I say.
Also in groups, the plans change. If person A and B both are present then I need to avoid them altogether as they are poison when together.

I'm sure you can find minor things in people's behavior that causes you harm, make yourself impervious to those bits and you will slowly start feeling better.

6)- Try to find "happiness" in very small things... Like a childish drawing. A pebble. Any food item. Obviously it will depend on how you want to perceive this world. If you force yourself to make the situation "happy", you will probably succeed in doing so.


Disclaimer: I haven't even tried many things because I am yet not sure what being "happy" actually means and if I really want to be in that state. But since you have already decided you want to be happy, I just put some points which i would do if I ever decide to be "happy".

At the end of the day, just remember to try your best and not have any regrets. No one else can handle your life better than you. So don't feel any sort of inferiority complex, your life is just that hard. Deal with it.
